'''Bharath Sriraman''' (born 1971) is an Indian-born Professor of Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of Montana–Missoula]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.umt.edu/sriraman/Admissions2009viewbook.pdf|title=Faculty Profile|publisher=University of Montana|access-date=18 June 2026|archive-date=31 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331003307/http://www.math.umt.edu/sriraman/Admissions2009viewbook.pdf|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref> and an academic editor,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616163011/http://archive.umt.edu/urelations/Report/2008/BharathSriraman.html |title=The University of Montana 2008 President's Report |publisher=Umt.edu |access-date=19 September 2026}}</ref> known for his contributions to the [[interdisciplinarity]] of mathematics-science-arts; visual, experimental and computational approaches to mathematics <ref>{{cite web|url=http://research.blog.umt.edu/post/83745161018/um-professor-interviewed-for-roeper-review|title=UM Professor Interviewed for Roeper Review |publisher=Umt.edu |access-date=10 November 2014}}</ref>, theory development and international overviews in [[mathematics education]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.umt.edu/news/2023/05/051623panl.php/|title=ICME-Plenary Panel Chair|publisher=University of Montana|access-date=16 May 2023}}</ref>. He has also contributed to  [[creativity]] research,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kaputcenter.org/2018/10/library-of-2015-2016-kaput-center-colloquium-talks/|title=Symposium: Mathematical Creativity- Musings from the Past Decade |date=9 October 2018 |publisher=Kaputcenter.umass.edu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817004639/http://kaputcenter.org/2018/10/library-of-2015-2016-kaput-center-colloquium-talks/ |access-date=22 February 2020|archive-date=17 August 2022 }}</ref> the history and [[philosophy of mathematics]],<ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-031-40846-5/ |title=Handbook of the History and Philosophy of Mathematical Practice |date=27 April 2024 |publisher=SpringerNature|doi=10.1007/978-3-031-40846-5 |isbn=978-3-031-40845-8 |access-date=26 May 2024 |editor-last1=Sriraman |editor-first1=Bharath }}</ref> and [[gifted education]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gazette.jhu.edu/2011/03/21/cty-math-minds-and-a-milestone/ |title=Study of Mathematically Precocious Youth 40th Anniversary Symposium|publisher=Johns Hopkins University |access-date=4 April 2012}}</ref>

==Education and honors==
Bharath Sriraman attended St. Michael’s School (founded by the [[Jesuits]] of [[St. Michael's Church, Mumbai]]) from 1976-87. He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in mathematics from the [[University of Alaska Fairbanks]] in 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.uaf.edu/alumnus-7/2/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170105181244/http://news.uaf.edu/alumnus-7/2/|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 January 2017|title=Class Notes|publisher=Aurora Alumni magazine|access-date=27 July 2010}}</ref> He obtained his [[Master of Science|M.S]] in Mathematics in 1999 followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Mathematical Sciences in 2002 both from [[Northern Illinois University]] under the functional analyst Robert Wheeler.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=3564|name=Robert Wheeler}}</ref> In 2009, Northern Illinois University named him as one of 50 "Golden alumni" in the last 50 years for his significant contributions to research in mathematics education, gifted education and interdisciplinary research at the intersection of mathematics-science-arts.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.niu.edu/clas50/50alumni/sriraman.shtml |archive-date=25 July 2010 |title=Archived copy |access-date=18 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100725033717/http://www.niu.edu/clas50/50alumni/sriraman.shtml |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> He previously received the School Science and Mathematics Association Early Scholar Award in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ssma.org/past-recipients |title=SSMA Past Award Recipients |publisher=ssma.org |access-date=13 July 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130714163934/http://www.ssma.org/past-recipients |archive-date=14 July 2013 }}</ref> In 2016 he was the recipient of the University of Montana Distinguished Scholar Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.umt.edu/2016/04/041916umrd.php|title=2016 UM Employee Day|publisher=umt.edu|access-date=9 August 2016|archive-date=1 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160801211053/http://news.umt.edu/2016/04/041916umrd.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the 15th International Congress on Mathematical Education (2024) in Sydney, he chaired the plenary panel on ''What counts as evidence in mathematics education'' <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://icme15.org/icme-15-scientific-program/icme-15-plenary-events/ |title=ICME 15 Plenary Events|publisher=icme15.org |access-date=6 August 2024}}</ref>

== Academic and editorial work ==
Sriraman is the founder and [[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[The Mathematics Enthusiast]]'', an independent [[open access journal]] hosted by University of Montana.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scholarworks.umt.edu/tme/ |title= The Mathematics Enthusiast|access-date=27 May 2015}}</ref> He is the co-founder/co-editor-in-chief of two series with [[Springer Science+Business Media]] namely ''[[Advances in Mathematics Education]]''<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/series/8392|title=Advances in Mathematics Education, Springer Heidelberg|publisher=springer.com |access-date=14 January 2016}}</ref> and ''[[Creativity Theory and Action in Education]]''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/series/13904|title=Creativity Theory and Action in Education, Springer Switzerland|publisher=springer.com |access-date=14 January 2016}}</ref> In addition to editing he is a prolific scholar with over 300 publications to date in numerous areas of research,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=YnPG9YoAAAAJ&hl=en|title= Google Scholar Papers|access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref> and held numerous visiting professorships including those as International Fulbright Specialist<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cies.org/grantee/bharath-sriraman|title=Fulbright Scholar Program|access-date=12 December 2018|archive-date=15 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215022128/https://www.cies.org/grantee/bharath-sriraman|url-status=dead}}</ref> at institutions in Nordic countries,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hi.is/search/allt/Sriraman|title=University of Iceland: Bharath Sriraman |access-date=22 February 2020}}</ref> Eurasia and South America.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.agenciacyta.org.ar/2012/06/“conceptualmente-la-matematica-es-mas-un-arte-que-una-ciencia”/|title=Conceptualmente la Matemática es más un arte que una ciencia |access-date=22 February 2020}}</ref> He also holds an adjunct appointment in the department of Central and Southwest-Asian Studies at the University of Montana<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hs.umt.edu/cswa/people/default.php|title=Central and Southwest Asia Program (CAP) |publisher=Umt.edu |access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.umt.edu/sriraman/central_asian.html|title=Central Asian Studies|publisher=University of Montana|access-date=13 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007032214/http://www.math.umt.edu/sriraman/central_asian.html|archive-date=7 October 2013}}</ref>
